outcome: Risk of severe cardiovascular complications after delivery
cohort: 1,165,684 women in Sweden from 2005 to 2017, including 140,128 women who delivered by cesarean section, 614,355 women who delivered vaginally, and 411,201 nulliparous women.
finding: Women who delivered by cesarean section had a 2.23 times higher risk of severe cardiovascular complications within 42 days of delivery compared to women who delivered vaginally.
mod_finding: Cesarean section delivery was associated with a doubling of the risk for severe cardiovascular events within 42 days of delivery.
